title: Alias Trace
statement: Implement `solve(ops)`. Two names, `a` and `b`, refer to the same list. `ops` is a list of `["append", who, value]` steps. Apply each append to that shared list. Return `{"a": [...], "b": [...]}` with the final contents. Because the names alias one list, both results are equal and contain every append, no matter which name was used.
constraints: who is the string a or b
hints: Start from one list and point both names at it.
Append on the list the name refers to. Do not copy between steps.
When you build the result dict, copy the list twice so each side is a snapshot of the same contents.
editorial: Assignment never copies a list. After b = a, an append through either name is visible through the other. The trace makes that concrete: the final contents depend on the shared object, not on which variable the source code mentioned.
